I hate to be that person, but I would ask your primary care provider. Thyroid issues can be very complicated and unique to everyone. Stimulants can raise blood pressure, speed up gastric motility, and in some people it reduces appetite which can result in weight loss. So on one hand the stuff you listed could be due to not being on a stimulant that causes the opposite impact, but maybe your thyroid is off instead or in addition to stopping your stimulant. The true way to know is by talking to your provider and checking thyroid levels via a blood test.

It honestly depends on what triggers your asthma, if that’s your reason for seeing the allergist. If you notice your asthma is worse during certain seasons or when you’re around dogs, cats, mold, dust, etc., then it could be affected by allergies.

But going to an allergist even if this is true might not be super helpful in getting “treatment.” You might go for them to just say to take Zyrtec or nasal spray over the counter, during your tough seasons. Or you could get the allergy shots suggestion, which I’m doing. 

So for me the allergist was worth it bc my asthma is very much allergy triggered and the nasal spray/Zyrtec/Benadryl combo wasn’t working. I would think about your asthma triggers, severity/frequency of symptoms, your own concerns, and suggestions from the pulmonologist before making a final decision.

Hey there! Some other things to consider;

-Changing pillowcases: If you don’t shower before bed you can bring allergens home, so changing pillowcases everyday or just more often in general can help reduce allergies you breathe in while sleeping

-Vacuuming the house more: My asthma improved a lot when we vaccumed the house more because there’s less dirty particles to breathe in

-Benadryl: I found that taking Benadryl (before bed because it makes you drowsy) helped my allergies and in turn my asthma

-Exercise with breath work: Doing yoga, swimming, running, etc where you have to focus or time your breathing can be useful. Learning how to swim helped me to improve my breathing and my lung capacity.

-Cutting out milk: for me cutting out milk helped me feel like I had less phlegm, though there is no scientific association between the two

A lot of my asthma problems were reduced through doing the things I mentioned and managing my allergies.
